info.title: xrelease API
info.description:
Self-hosted release notifier — management API and inbound webhooks.

Started with `xrelease serve`. Polling continues in the background; webhooks provide low-latency push for GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Codeberg, Bitbucket, and Docker Hub.

Configuration is split: `bootstrap.toml` (infra) + desired state (sources / teams / notifiers via file, API ledger, or UI Apply). Notifiers include Apprise, Novu, Slack, Telegram, SMTP, webhooks, eXpress, and optional brokers.

Source kinds (`type`): `github`, `codeberg`, `gitea`, `gitlab`, `bitbucket`, `docker`, `ghcr`, `quay`, `ecr`, `feed`, `pypi`, `npm`, `yarn`, `cargo`, `maven`, `nuget`, `hex`, `rubygems`, `packagist`, `cpan`, `artifacthub`.

post.summary: Link a local user to SSO by email (or pin an OIDC subject)
post.description: Admin-only. Set `email` to the address the IdP will assert; the opaque `oidc_sub` binds itself on that person's first OIDC sign-in, provided the token carries `email_verified`. This is the normal path — an admin provisioning an account ahead of first login knows the address but not the subject. Blank/null `email` clears the link and any bound subject; changing the address also clears it, so the new address must be proven again. `oidc_sub` may still be sent to pin or clear a subject directly. `auth_source` stays `local`, so password login keeps working.

post.summary: Re-read the app config file and hot-swap it
post.description: File-mode counterpart of /api/v1/config/apply: takes no body and re-reads the configured app config file (--app / XRELEASE_APP_CONFIG), validates it, and hot-swaps sources, notifiers, and teams. Returns 409 when a config ledger revision is authoritative (use /api/v1/config/apply instead) and 400 when no app config file is configured. Also triggered by SIGHUP.

get.description: Newest-first page of the config revision ledger. Returns metadata only — revision bodies are deliberately omitted so this endpoint cannot bypass the secret redaction applied by GET /api/v1/config. Includes rejected apply attempts and their errors. `applied_by` is the server-verified principal (`api_key`, `oidc:<sub>`), optionally annotated with a client-supplied X-Config-Applied-By label in parentheses.

get.summary: What the desired-state config accepts (for UI controls)
get.description: Machine-readable option lists so a UI can render selects, a sink picker, a team-tag multi-select and a schedule widget instead of a raw config text box. Includes `sink_kinds` (every sink is available), `team_tags` / `preset_names` (running config), and `config_authority` (`[config_api].source`). `readonly_sections` are bootstrap-only and rejected in any pushed document. `template_placeholders` documents the notifier Mustache dialect.

bearerAuth.description: Static API key (`[api].api_key` / `XRELEASE_API_KEY`) or OIDC access token JWT (`[api.oidc]` / `XRELEASE_OIDC_ISSUER`). Required when either auth method is configured.

notifiers_ok.description: Configured sinks report healthy. Apprise uses a live HTTP probe; other sinks (SMTP, webhook, brokers) are presence-based so transient blips do not flap readiness — delivery failures appear in the outbox metrics.

oidc_sub.description: OIDC subject (`sub`) when the user is linked to an IdP identity. Omitted when unset.

last_login_at.description: Last successful login. Omitted when the user has never signed in.

organization_roles.description: Per-organization role grants from OIDC scoped aliases (e.g. xrelease-admin:platform). Omitted when empty.

email.description: SSO link key — the address the IdP will assert for this person. The opaque subject binds itself on their first OIDC sign-in, provided the token carries `email_verified`. Blank/null clears the link and any bound subject. Changing the address also clears the bound subject.

oidc_sub.description: IdP subject to attach. Null or blank unlinks SSO from the local user.

oidc_auto_create_users.description: Whether an unknown OIDC subject is provisioned on first sign-in (`[api.oidc] auto_create_users`). When false the user directory is an allow-list.

role.description: Instance-wide role. Api-key principals are always admin.

organization_roles.description: Per-organization grants from OIDC scoped aliases (admin:platform). Empty for local and api-key.
